IN.name: India
IN.plug: Type C, D and M (230 V)
tips: Carry a digital and printed copy of your ID; hotels and many trains ask for it.
Download offline maps and keep some cash, as small towns and hill areas can have patchy UPI/network.
Book trains early (open ~60 days ahead), especially for weekends and festivals.

emergency.note: 112 is the all-in-one emergency number across India. Numbers can vary slightly by state.

AE.name: United Arab Emirates
AE.visa: Check the current rules for Indian passport holders (visa on arrival or e-visa conditions can change).
tips: Dress modestly in malls, mosques and public areas; public displays of affection can be a problem.
Carrying or importing medicines needs checking: some common drugs are controlled, so keep prescriptions.
Alcohol rules are strict, so drink only at licensed venues.

emergency.note: Dubai Police also take non-emergency calls on 901.

SG.name: Singapore
SG.visa: Check the current e-visa/entry rules for Indian passport holders; arrival cards are filled online (SG Arrival Card).
tips: Rules are strict: no chewing gum import, heavy fines for littering and smoking in banned areas.
Vapes are banned.
Tap with a contactless bank card on MRT and buses.

TH.name: Thailand
TH.plug: Types A, B, C and O (230 V)
TH.language: Thai and English in tourist areas
TH.visa: Check the current visa-exemption/e-visa rules for Indian passport holders; arrival forms (TDAC) are submitted online.
tips: Respect the monarchy and dress modestly at temples (cover shoulders and knees).
Use metered taxis or ride-hailing; agree prices upfront for tuk-tuks.
If renting a scooter, check your licence and insurance cover.

ID.name: Indonesia
ID.visa: Check visa-on-arrival/e-VOA rules for Indian passport holders and the Bali tourist levy (paid online).
tips: Dress and behave respectfully at temples; sarongs are often provided.
Drink bottled or filtered water.
Scooter accidents are common; if you ride, use a helmet and check your insurance covers it.

MY.name: Malaysia
MY.visa: Check the current visa-free/e-visa rules for Indian passport holders; fill in the MDAC digital arrival card.
tips: Dress modestly at mosques and temples.
Use ride-hailing apps or meters; avoid unmetered taxis.
Malaysia has strict drug laws, with severe penalties.

emergency.note: 999 works from landlines and mobiles; 112 also connects from a mobile phone.

NP.name: Nepal
NP.currency: Nepalese rupee (NPR); Indian ₹100 and smaller notes are commonly accepted (check current rules)
NP.plug: Types C, D and M (230 V)
NP.visa: Indian citizens can usually enter without a visa, but carry accepted photo ID (passport or voter ID) and check the current rules.
tips: Altitude sickness can affect treks above ~2,500 m; ascend slowly.
Power cuts and traffic are common; add buffer time to schedules.
₹500 and ₹2000 notes are not allowed; carry ₹100 and smaller notes.

LK.name: Sri Lanka
LK.plug: Types D, G and M (230 V)
LK.visa: Check the current visa/ETA rules for Indian passport holders before booking.
tips: Dress modestly at temples and remove shoes and hats.
Use metered tuk-tuks or ride-hailing; agree fares in advance.
Never pose with your back to a Buddha statue.

MV.name: Maldives
MV.currency: Maldivian rufiyaa (MVR); US dollars widely used at resorts
MV.plug: Types D, G and J (230 V)
MV.visa: Entry is typically on a free tourist visa on arrival, with a confirmed booking and onward ticket; check current rules.
tips: Alcohol is only available at resorts; local islands have dress and behaviour rules.
Pork and drone use are restricted; read the rules before packing.
Book speedboat/seaplane transfers and ferry timings in advance.

FR.name: France
FR.visa: Schengen short-stay visa; insurance with at least €30,000 medical cover is required. Book your appointment early.
tips: Pickpocketing is common near major sights and on the metro; use a cross-body bag.
Greet with 'Bonjour' before asking anything in shops and cafés.
Validate your metro ticket and keep it until you exit.

JP.name: Japan
JP.visa: A short-stay visa is needed for Indian passport holders; e-visa options may be available. Check the current process.
tips: Carry some cash: many small shops and temples are cash-only.
No tipping, and eating while walking is frowned upon.
Many common medicines (e.g. some cold medicines) are restricted; check before carrying.

emergency.note: Ask for English support when you call; the operator can connect an interpreter.

TR.name: Türkiye
TR.visa: Check the current e-visa eligibility for Indian passport holders, which can depend on a valid US/UK/Schengen visa or residence permit.
tips: Agree the price first or insist on the meter in taxis.
Dress modestly in mosques and carry a scarf.
Carry a copy of your passport; keep the original in the hotel safe.

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.visa: A Standard Visitor visa is needed for Indian passport holders; apply well ahead.
tips: Tap in and out with a contactless card or Oyster on the Tube and buses.
Pre-book big attractions and the Harry Potter studio tour.
Travel insurance with healthcare cover is strongly advised, since NHS care for visitors can be charged.
